data.hypothesis: The measured parent is correct and substantially faster than the serial baseline, but its OpenMP if-clause still expresses small-input execution as a serialized parallel region. An explicit serial branch below the existing 128-element threshold may avoid that runtime overhead while retaining the same bounded, statically scheduled parallel loop for larger inputs; the controller must measure whether this affects small cases or official-workload throughput.

memory_lessons.applicability: This establishes a useful reference for further OpenMP experiments on this kernel, but does not predict the effect of the proposed explicit serial branch.
memory_lessons.claim: The parent OpenMP candidate was valid on all 8 reported cases and measured 0.0706517 seconds versus the serial baseline's 0.3900794 seconds; the new branch has not been measured.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure this explicit serial fallback against the selected parent on both small sizes and the official workload.

data.notes: Existing controller measurements report the baseline at 0.390079 seconds and the selected parent at 0.070652 seconds (three samples each), approximately 5.52x faster; both are reported valid. Parent correctness covered n=16, 128, 1024 and 131072. This candidate has no measurements yet. The helper keeps the per-option arithmetic order and its scratch array local; both paths write each result element.
transformations: Extracted the unchanged per-option binomial arithmetic into a static inline helper with local scratch storage.
Replaced the OpenMP if-clause with an explicit serial fallback for counts below 128 or a one-thread budget, avoiding an OpenMP parallel construct on that path.
Kept static OpenMP worksharing for larger counts and bounded the requested team size by the positive threads argument and count.
